name: payload-identical-across-restart

graded_by.test: harness/rigs/kill-core.sh with the ttyrec differ — a recording across kill -9 of the core is payload-identical to an uninterrupted run, and monotonic per direction
core/internal/session/reattach_test.go — a reattach replays from last_committed_seq + 1 and records no output payload twice and none lost

description: The E1 gate's comparator (phase-01: recording across the restart payload-identical to an uninterrupted run, timestamps monotonic across the seam; x-compare). Per direction the concatenated payloads of the data frames are byte-equal; frame boundaries may differ — here the restart split one output frame in two, and the replay kept each part's own stamp — and the end markers are left out, so two different end times do not matter; neither recording declares a loss, so their gap markers (none) are the same. Byte-identical is unachievable once worker-owned timestamps are compared, and vacuous if they are not. A recording with a gap marker is never payload-identical to one without: the gap is declared, not closed.
